Basic Guidelines for Adding Images Only images that have been uploaded to the WikiDoc platform can be used. To upload an image, navigate to the designated upload page. Once uploaded, the image will appear in the image list. For proper usage, refer to the WikiDoc image use policy. All information provided on this page is attributed to Wikipedia and its contributors. Detailed Instructions for Image Insertion and Syntax Image Types 1. Thumbnail or Thumb: The image is resized to a standard width, typically 180 pixels by default, unless a specific width is defined by the user. A border is automatically added around the image. If a caption is provided, it will appear below the image. By default, the image is aligned to the right unless the Location attribute is used to override this setting. 2. Frame: The image retains its original size, and a border is added around it. If a caption is provided, it will appear below the image. 3. No Type Specified: The image retains its original size, and no border is added. If a caption is provided, it will not be displayed. 4. Border: Similar to the No Type Specified option, but a border is added around the image. Image Placement (Location) 1. Right: The image, along with its border or box, is positioned on the right side of the page. The text following the image flows around it. 2. Left: The image, along with its border or box, is positioned on the left side of the page. The text following the image flows around it. 3. Center: The image, along with its border or box, is centered on the page. The text following the image is placed below it. 4. None: The image, along with its border or box, is positioned on the left side of the page. The text following the image is placed below it. Image Sizing 1. Fixed Width (e.g., 100px): The image is resized to a width of 100 pixels. You can replace 100 with any desired value. If both thumbnail and a specific size are defined, the specified size takes precedence. If the original image is smaller than the specified size, it will remain at its original dimensions. 2. Fixed Dimensions (e.g., 100x200px): The image is resized to a maximum width of 100 pixels and a maximum height of 200 pixels. The original aspect ratio of the image is preserved. Captions Any text that does not match a recognized attribute (e.g., size, location) is treated as caption text. Advanced Syntax for Image Insertion The updated syntax for inserting images is backward-compatible, meaning existing articles do not need to be modified. The syntax allows for multiple options to be specified, which control the placement, size, and presentation of the image. These options include: Placement: right, left, center, none Size: sizepx (e.g., 200px) Type: thumbnail (thumb), frame Caption Text: alternate text or descriptive text Options are separated by vertical bars (|) and can be listed in any order. If an unrecognized option is included, it is treated as caption text. If multiple unrecognized options are present, the last one takes precedence. Thumbnail Features A small enlarge icon is displayed in the lower margin of the thumbnail. Both the image and the icon link to the image description page, where the image can be viewed at its original size. The hover text for the icon always displays Enlarge, even if the image is already at its maximum size. Inline Image Rendering When no options other than size or caption text are specified, the image is rendered inline with the surrounding text. Linking to an Image Description Page To create a link to the description page of an image, use a leading colon before image: in the intra-wiki link. For example: ``` [[:image:example.jpg]] ``` This will generate a link to the image description page. Creating Image Galleries To display multiple images in a gallery format: Images are displayed in a larger size. The entire gallery is centered on the page. Example: Two-Image Gallery A similar gallery format can be used for displaying two images side by side. Additional Caption Formatting Captions can include additional formatting, such as bold or italic text. For example: ``` '''Bold Caption Text''' ``` All standard text formatting options are supported.
